text: Let's cover the layer between raw tables and an actual report — semantic models.

Trips and zones are two separate tables, with no defined relationship and no agreed business definitions. A semantic model adds exactly that — relationships, measures, and friendly names — so a report author queries concepts, not raw columns.

A relationship connects trips to zones the same way a join would in PySpark, just defined once, in the model, instead of repeated in every query. A measure is a named calculation, defined once, so two report authors never accidentally define total revenue two different ways.
And this is actually where Direct Lake mode lives — not a report setting, but a property of the semantic model itself. Relationships and measures apply right on top of that fast, direct read.
Concepts, not raw columns, defined once. Next lesson: Fabric capacities and SKUs, the real pricing tiers, named.
